note: Curated map from a matter's issue tags (doctrine slugs) to LSAT reasoning concepts. Every concept id is validated against the concept catalog at import; an unknown id is a hard error, not a silent skip. Add entries as matters use tags the map does not cover — `unmapped_tags` in the study-plan response is the to-do list.

contract-formation.label: Contract formation
contract-formation.why: Offer, acceptance and consideration are conditional rules: whether a contract exists is a chain of if-then tests, which is exactly the reasoning LR conditionals drill.

contract-interpretation.label: Contract interpretation
contract-interpretation.why: Reading a disputed clause is close reading against context — the RC skill set.

breach-of-contract.label: Breach of contract
breach-of-contract.why: A breach argument stands or falls on whether the alleged facts satisfy the promise; testing that is sufficient/necessary condition work.

negligence.label: Negligence
negligence.why: Duty, breach, causation and damages is a four-element test whose hard element is causation — the classic cause-and-correlation trap.

causation.label: Causation
causation.why: But-for and proximate cause are the legal names for the reasoning LR tests as alternative causes and reversed causation.

damages.label: Damages
damages.why: Quantum arguments turn on rates, totals and samples, where percent-vs-number errors live.

statutory-interpretation.label: Statutory interpretation
statutory-interpretation.why: Applying a statute to facts is rule application plus scope discipline: what the text does and does not reach.

constitutional-law.label: Constitutional law
constitutional-law.why: Tiered scrutiny is principle application; the doctrinal debates are argument-structure questions.

civil-procedure.label: Civil procedure
civil-procedure.why: Jurisdiction and joinder rules are constraint satisfaction — the same machinery as a logic game.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.why: Admissibility is a rule with exceptions and exceptions to exceptions; inference limits are what MSS questions test.

criminal-law.label: Criminal law
criminal-law.why: Mens rea and actus reus are conjunctive elements; defenses are counterarguments to be answered on their own terms.

property.label: Property
property.why: Estates and future interests are ordering problems with strict rules — sequencing, done in legal vocabulary.

employment.label: Employment
employment.why: Discrimination claims are burden-shifting frameworks: each step is a sufficient or necessary showing, and pretext arguments are alternative-cause arguments.

landlord-tenant.label: Landlord and tenant
landlord-tenant.why: Habitability and notice rules are conditionals with deadlines; the disputes are paradoxes of who did what when.

administrative-law.label: Administrative law
administrative-law.why: Deference doctrines are arguments about how an argument should be evaluated — method and role questions.

appeals.label: Appeals
appeals.why: An appellate brief is an argument about an argument: standard of review, preserved error, and the shape of the reasoning below.

legal-writing.label: Legal writing
legal-writing.why: The writing section rehearses exactly what a brief needs: a position, its warrant, and an honest answer to the other side.
